action.rationale: Fresh problem (dim=50) with full budget remaining (100 evals) and cheap, deterministic evaluations; per policy we should learn the landscape first. Probes cost ~12% of the budget and populate the archive, guiding whether to use TuRBO/CMA-ES or a local solver next.

Probes on this 50-D, cheap, deterministic problem are ambiguous (P2 fdc_spearman=0.21; top10_spread_vs_uniform≈1.01), so we should hedge between global CMA-ES and local trust-region TuRBO. With 88 evals left, allocating 28 to a race preserves most of the budget while identifying the better performer.

With 50D and only 60 evals left, the initial race (14 evals each) had both CMA-ES (621.297) and TuRBO (621.471) fail to beat the probe incumbent 620.958, and there’s been a 36-eval stall. CMA-ES’ current setup (popsize 15, sigma 2.90) is likely too slow for the remaining budget, while TuRBO typically performs better in high-D, small-budget regimes when warm-started from the archive.
